title: Bounded reverse field copying
statement: For every natural number $m$, there are a finite state set $P$ with decidable equality, a two-work-tape machine $R$ over an arbitrary symbol type $\Gamma$, designated states $entry,exit\in P$, and a natural number $C$ such that the following holds. For every input word $x$, list of fields $fs$ of length $m$, and configuration $d$ on input $x$, suppose $d$ begins in state $entry$, tape $1$ contains the joined fields in the specified field-tape representation at offsets from $-1$ through the total joined length relative to its head, and tape $0$ is blank throughout those offsets. Then in some time $t\le C(L+1)$, where $L$ is the length of the joined fields, the machine reaches a configuration equal to $d$ except that its state is $exit$ and tape $0$ contains the joined fields in field-tape representation on the interval of length $L$ starting at its initial head position. It does not visit $exit$ earlier, and both tape heads remain within distance $C(L+1)$ of their initial positions through time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite state set $P$ with decidable equality exists
Two work tapes and arbitrary symbol type $\Gamma$
Tape $1$ satisfies the RecordAt condition for $fs$
Tape $0$ is blank over the specified interval
Both head displacement bounds through time $t$
Final configuration with copied joined fields on tape $0$
